paragraphs: In Rotherham, children in care are looked after by Fostering Rotherham, the not-for-profit fostering service run by Rotherham Metropolitan Borough Council, alongside the independent fostering agencies listed on this page. The council's Looked After Children and Care Leavers Sufficiency Strategy 2023 to 2028 sets out an aim to increase the number of approved in-house foster carers and to help more young people aged 10 and over to live safely in families within their own communities.

Fostering Rotherham offers several kinds of fostering. Short-term, task-centred care can last from a single night to as long as two years while plans are made for a child's future. Emergency carers take children in at short notice, usually for a few days, and long-term carers give children who cannot go home a settled family, often until they reach adulthood. Second home care provides short breaks, and Level Four carers look after children with additional needs, disabilities or more complex emotional needs, with specialist training in therapeutic parenting.

On support, the council describes help that is available around the clock, a social worker alongside you during assessment, a personalised handbook once you are approved and a buddy scheme that pairs you with an experienced carer. There are three Mockingbird hubs offering regular respite, along with free support groups for foster families. Carers receive training in managing different behaviours, and the service also offers 14 days of paid leave a year and 40p a mile for journeys made for a child.

Payments are made up of a fee, which rises with your skill level, plus an allowance for the child's needs. Published pages do not give a timescale for assessment, so it is worth asking directly. A sensible next step is to speak to Fostering Rotherham and two or three of the agencies listed below, and compare the training, support and pay each one offers.

sources.title: Looked After Children and Care Leavers Sufficiency Strategy 2023-2028 (Rotherham Council)
